locus: Theses in quibus exponitur An & quatenus homo per Christi gratiam Legem implere possit, & Dei mandata servare, I-XVIII (man created able to obey the law perfectly (Eccl. 7:29); fallen man cannot keep it of himself (Eph. 2; John 15; 2 Cor. 3; Rom. 8); Christ frees from sin's slavery as well as its penalty; the new-covenant grace promised in Ezekiel 11 and 36, Jeremiah 31-32 and Deuteronomy 30; keeping the commandments required for salvation and communion with Christ (Psalm 103; Ezekiel 18; Revelation 22; 1 John 2, 3, 5; 1 Cor. 7:19); the saints kept them (Psalm 119; Luke 1:6) and they are not burdensome (1 John 5:3); in a true sense the regenerate fulfil the law (Rom. 13; Rom. 8:3-4); but none fulfils it perfectly, by the strict rule of 'Do this and live' and its curse (Gal. 3:10; Rom. 4), since all have sinned (Rom. 3), the holiest sin daily (Jas. 3:2; 1 John 1:8; Eccl. 7:20), and the regenerate fall into grave sins (David, Peter)).
